headline: crvUSD core contracts verified on Etherscan with multiple recognized-firm audits; most recent ChainSecurity review dated February 2025 covers updated stablecoin contracts

findings.text: The Emergency DAO Safe (0x467947...) is confirmed verified on Etherscan (abiSource: 'etherscan') with its proxy implementation (0x34CfAC646f301356fAa8B21e94227e3583Fe3F5F — Gnosis Safe 1.3.0) also resolvable via DeFiPunkd. All crvUSD core contracts listed in the official deployment docs (crvUSD token 0xf939E0A0..., Controller Factory 0xC9332fdC..., Controller Implementation 0xe3e3Fb7E..., AMM Implementation 0x2B7e624b..., PriceAggregator, PriceAggregatorV3, FlashLender, PegKeepersV1/V2, and all market Controllers/AMMs) are linked with '#code' anchors on Etherscan in the official docs, indicating source verification is present for each.

Public source repo at https://github.com/curvefi/curve-stablecoin confirmed active with 2,955 commits, Vyper (35.1%) + Python (64.1%). Docs cross-link this repo for all crvUSD contracts. No commit SHA was pinned in this run; bytecode diff not performed — recorded in unknowns.

Multiple audits of crvUSD-related contracts identified from the official audit page: (1) MixBytes, June 5 2023 (Curve Stablecoin/crvUSD initial); (2) ChainSecurity, January 24 2024 (Curve Stablecoin update); (3) ChainSecurity, December 12 2023 (crvUSD PegKeeperV2); (4) StateMind, February 2 2024 (Curve Lending); (5) ChainSecurity, February 21 2025 (Curve Stablecoin — most recent, covers OneWayLendingFactory, TwoWayLendingFactory, Controller, AMM, monetary policy, peg keepers); (6) ChainSecurity, December 3 2024 (Savings crvUSD / scrvUSD). The most recent ChainSecurity review (Feb 2025) is within 15 months of this analysis date.

Auditors are ChainSecurity (a broadly-recognized Solidity/Vyper firm), MixBytes (recognized), and StateMind (recognized). All three are listed as recognized in the rubric or are established DeFi auditors with public track records on major protocols.

The most recent audit (ChainSecurity, February 21 2025) covers updated crvUSD stablecoin contracts including changes to OneWayLendingFactory, TwoWayLendingFactory, and monetary policy. No diff between the Feb 2025 audit commit and the current deployed bytecode was sampled in this run — recorded in unknowns. The repo has 2,955 commits and is actively maintained.

The Emergency DAO Safe (0x467947...) is a proxy pointing to Gnosis Safe singleton 0x34CfAC646f301356fAa8B21e94227e3583Fe3F5F, confirmed via DeFiPunkd. Docs state implementation contracts (Controller, AMM) are upgradeable blueprints. The DeFiPunkd surfacer confirmed ABI source is 'etherscan' for the Safe proxy, indicating both proxy and implementation are verified. For the upgradeable Controller/AMM blueprint contracts, verification links in the docs deployment page use '#code' anchors, indicating those are also verified on Etherscan.

steelman.red: crvUSD uses factory-deployed blueprint contracts whose individual market deployments are permissionlessly created; not all blueprint instances may be independently verified, and no local bytecode compile was run to confirm equivalence between Etherscan-uploaded source and deployed bytecode.
steelman.orange: The repo is actively updated (2,955 commits) and no commit SHA was pinned to tie the latest deployed bytecode to the Feb 2025 audit scope; some drift between audit commit and current master is likely, and StateMind was used for lending while the main stablecoin's most recent audit is from Feb 2025 (~15 months before analysis date).
steelman.green: All named core contracts appear verified on Etherscan (docs link '#code' for each), there is a public Vyper source repo with active history, and three recognized firms (ChainSecurity, MixBytes, StateMind) have collectively covered the crvUSD stablecoin, PegKeeperV2, lending markets, and scrvUSD—with the most recent ChainSecurity review in February 2025 covering the currently-deployed stablecoin contracts.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because: the official deployment page cross-links Etherscan '#code' anchors for every listed core contract and market contract, confirming bytecode verification; the source is publicly available in a recognized repo (curvefi/curve-stablecoin); and three recognized audit firms (ChainSecurity, MixBytes, StateMind) have collectively reviewed the deployed crvUSD system with the most recent audit in February 2025. The orange steelman (unverified drift since Feb 2025) is weaker because the Feb 2025 ChainSecurity report explicitly covers the current deployed contract versions (OneWayLendingFactory, TwoWayLendingFactory, updated Controller/AMM/monetary policy), and no specific post-audit material changes were identified in this run—only general repo activity was noted.

protocol_metadata.about: crvUSD is Curve Finance's native CDP stablecoin on Ethereum, allowing users to mint crvUSD by depositing crypto collateral (wstETH, sfrxETH, wBTC, ETH, tBTC, cbBTC, LBTC, weETH) into individual per-collateral markets. Each market has its own Controller and LLAMMA AMM contract that performs continuous soft-liquidations via a lending-liquidating AMM mechanism, reducing sharp liquidation events. The system is governed by the Curve DAO through an Aragon ownership vote with a ~7-day timelock, with an Emergency DAO 5-of-9 multisig able to pause individual markets immediately.
